title: Mini CRUD Task Tracker
description: Build a tiny task-tracking web app with a React or plain-JS frontend, a REST API, and a relational database. Keep scope to create/read/update/delete tasks and a minimal responsive UI.

rubric.criterion: Create, read, update and delete operations all work end-to-end.
Tasks persist in a relational database and are not only stored in browser memory.
A documented REST endpoint is used between UI and backend.
The interface remains usable on a narrow mobile viewport.
Repository contains a README with setup/run instructions and a clear project structure.

title: Containerize and CI-check a Web Service
description: Take a tiny HTTP service, containerize it with Docker, and add a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the image and runs a basic smoke test. Deployment can use a free-tier/cloud sandbox if available, but the CI artifact is mandatory.

rubric.criterion: A working Dockerfile is present and builds successfully.
A .github/workflows/*.yml CI workflow file is present and runs on push or pull request.
CI starts or checks the service and verifies a successful HTTP response.
README documents local build/run commands and the architecture in brief.
No secret keys or credentials are committed to the repository.

title: Public-Dataset Classifier
description: Train a simple classifier on a public tabular dataset, evaluate it with at least two appropriate metrics, and explain the result and limitations in the README. Keep the model classical; no deep-learning requirement.

rubric.criterion: Notebook runs top to bottom without error from a clean kernel.
A supervised classifier is trained on a public dataset with a documented train/test split.
At least two relevant evaluation metrics are reported and interpreted.
README explains the dataset, model choice, main result and at least one limitation.
Dependencies or environment instructions are recorded in the repository.

title: Messy Dataset to Three Insights
description: Take a public CSV with missing, inconsistent or duplicated values; clean it with pandas/SQL, make three clear visualizations, and write three evidence-backed insights for a non-technical reader.

rubric.criterion: Notebook runs top to bottom without error and produces the final tables/charts.
Cleaning steps explicitly address at least two real data-quality issues found in the dataset.
At least three appropriate visualizations are included and labeled.
Exactly three documented insights cite the underlying fields/aggregations supporting them.
README or report explains limitations and avoids claiming causation from descriptive analysis alone.
